messages.subject: Async programming in Shiny
parts:
Hello everyone,

I had to create a new post. I did not find any post that has already covered the new shiny feature: asynchronous programming.

I tested this new feature and I think I understood how it works. However, I still have an issue. See below of my application's code.

library(shiny)
library(promises)
library(future)
plan(multiprocess)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("refresh_data","refresh_data"),
  tableOutput("table"),
  sliderInput("obs", "Number of observations", 0, 1000, 500),
  actionButton("goButton", "Go!"),
  plotOutput("distPlot")
)

read.csv.long <- function(url){
    Sys.sleep(60)
    data = read.csv(url) 
}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  observe({
    url = "https://rstudio.github.io/promises/data.csv"
    
    data <- eventReactive(input$refresh_data, {
      future(read.csv.long(url))
    })
    
    
    output$table <- renderTable({
      data() %...>% head(5)
    })
    
    data2 <- eventReactive(input$goButton, {
      future({
        isolate(rnorm(input$obs))
      })
    })
    
    output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
      
       data2() %...>% hist()
    })
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


In this application, I have two button, one that allows me to perform a long operation and the other that allows to perform a quick operation. These two operations are executed asynchronously.
My goal is to launch my long operation then during this time to visualize my histogram (short operation). All this on the same web page.
Problem is I can not do it. I have to wait until long operation is completed before I can view my histogram.
On the other hand when I opened my page in a new tab, I can visualize my histogram while long operation is running (but that's not what I want to do)

Is it possible to do that ? Can you help me?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Async programming in Shiny
parts:
Thanks for the question. You may find better/faster answers these days if you visit the Shiny section of community.rstudio.com; we don't monitor this mailing list actively anymore.

1. There's no need to wrap all of your server code in an observe({ ... })
2. What you're describing is by design, but I've received a lot of feedback that it's not desirable. The rationale is described here: https://rstudio.github.io/promises/articles/shiny.html#the-flush-cycle

You can work around this by "hiding" the long-running operation from Shiny's flush cycle. Shiny only knows about promises if they are returned as the last expression of an observer (or reactive expression). You can change this code:

data <- eventReactive(input$refresh_data, {
      future(read.csv.long(url))
    })
    
    
    output$table <- renderTable({
      data() %...>% head(5)
    })

To something like this:

    data <- reactiveVal(NULL)

    observeEvent(input$refresh_data, {
      future(read.csv.long(url)) %...>%
        data() # Assign the resulting value to the `data` reactiveVal
    }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

    output$table <- renderTable({
      req(data()) %...>% head(5)
    })
